gaps.sentence: Their ___ was celebrated with a big party (MARRY).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'Their'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'marry' is 'marriage' (-age); an adjective cannot follow 'Their' as subject.

gaps.sentence: The company is a major ___ (EMPLOY) in the region.
gaps.hint: the company gives jobs — it is the one who employs
gaps.explanation: An employer gives work; an employee receives it. The sentence is about the company.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: Being blamed for something you didn't do is completely ___ (FAIR).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'is', and the situation is negative: unfair (un- + fair).

gaps.sentence: The instructions were unclear, so I had to ___ them completely (WRITE).
gaps.hint: write again — unclear the first time (re-); base verb needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rewrite. A base verb is needed after 'had to'.

gaps.sentence: It is ___ to book tickets in advance during the festival (ADVICE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -able forms the adjective: advisable means worth recommending. 'It is + adjective + to-infinitive'.
After 'in' a noun is needed: excitement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: She gave a very ___ account of the incident that had everyone laughing (HUMOUR).
gaps.explanation: Everyone laughed, so the adjective is humorous (-ous). 'Humourless' means serious and would contradict the laughter.
